problem.text: Triangle $GRT$ has $\overline{GR} = 5$, $\overline{RT} = 12$, and $\overline{GT} = 13$. The perpendicular bisector of $\overline{GT}$ intersects the extension $\overline{GR}$ at $O$. Find $\overline{TO}$.

steps.title: Where to start: spot the right angles
steps.body: There is no picture, so draw one. The sides $5$, $12$, $13$ are a famous Pythagorean triple, so $\triangle GRT$ has a right angle. The perpendicular bisector gives a second right angle: let $M$ be the midpoint of $GT$, so $MG = MT = \tfrac{13}{2}$ and $\angle OMT = 90^\circ$. Two right triangles sharing an angle is the classic setup for similar triangles.

your_turn.prompt: Which angle of $\triangle GRT$ is the right angle, and why?
your_turn.answer: $\angle R$, because $5^2 + 12^2 = 25 + 144 = 169 = 13^2$ and $GT = 13$ is the side opposite $R$.

steps.title: Where $O$ is, and the shared angle
steps.body: Triangles $MOT$ and $MOG$ share side $MO$, have $MT = MG$ and both have a right angle at $M$, so they are congruent (SAS). So $OT = OG$ and $\angle MTO = \angle MGO$. Now $O$ lies on line $GR$ extended past $R$, so ray $GO$ is ray $GR$ and $\angle MGO$ is just $\angle TGR$ of the original triangle.

your_turn.prompt: Why must $O$ be on the $R$ side of $G$ and not on the extension beyond $G$?
your_turn.answer: In right triangle $GMO$ the angle at $G$ must be acute. On ray $GR$ that angle is $\angle TGR$, which is acute; on the opposite ray it would be $180^\circ - \angle TGR$, which is obtuse.

steps.title: Two similar right triangles
steps.body: $\triangle TMO$ has a right angle at $M$ and angle $\angle MTO = \angle TGR$ at $T$. $\triangle GRT$ has a right angle at $R$ and the same angle at $G$. By AA, $\triangle TMO \sim \triangle GRT$, with $T \leftrightarrow G$, $M \leftrightarrow R$, $O \leftrightarrow T$.

your_turn.prompt: Using that matching, which side of $\triangle GRT$ corresponds to $TO$, and which corresponds to $TM$?
your_turn.answer: $TO$ matches the hypotenuse $GT$, and $TM$ matches $GR$ (the leg next to the equal angle).

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body:
Corresponding sides are in proportion:
$$\frac{TO}{TM} = \frac{GT}{GR} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad TO = \frac{13}{2}\cdot\frac{13}{5} = \frac{169}{10}.$$
This is bigger than $GR = 5$, so $O$ is indeed past $R$. The answer is **$\frac{169}{10}$**.
